title: Manunkquiaug
summary: Manunkquiaug is a Montauk placename in the North Neck area, near Great Pond, now Lake Montauk. It appears as a boundary point in a 1670 Montauk deed.
address_label: General eastern/southern Great Pond (Lake Montauk) boundary area
map_geometry_source: Approximate Great Pond / Lake Montauk boundary area based on Tooker entry 153; coordinate is not an exact deed boundary point.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Manunkquiaug, Manunkquinaug, Manunkquiag, Manunkguiaug, and M'anunkqua-auke. The name is interpreted as as far as the land goes or end of the land.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names play a crucial role in navigation, communication, and the establishment of a sense of identity and history for various places.”

— South Australian Department for Housing and Urban Development, Place names FAQs (2026), What are place names?

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
whereintheworld_content: Manunkquiaug is associated broadly with the eastern or southern Great Pond, now Lake Montauk. The exact boundary point named in the 1670 deed remains uncertain.
